scope: Standard ordinary/aligned byte ownership and reallocation over the shared unchanged raw heap backend; allocator callable reconciliation
source_capture_scope: 306 selected allocator/container/Standard sources, affected tests and oracle inputs; not a complete workspace compiler-input capture

behavior: StandardMemory no longer uses Vec storage. StandardByteStorage owns its original raw pointer and exact logical length; Allocate(0), AllocateOptimal(0), AllocateAligned(0,alignment) and Reallocate(nullptr,0) retain distinct real live allocations and native minimum alignment.

The existing raw_heap backend moved into Standard with only crate-private visibility widening. NCollection retains a private compatibility alias, preserving every allocation/header/reallocation/free operation and all pending canonical IBlock imports without duplicate arithmetic.

Standard byte owners call that backend directly and retain no BaseAllocator handle. No CommonBaseAllocator initialization or reference-count side effect is introduced, and no constructor recursion is possible through that singleton.

Positive Reallocate uses the shared raw realloc operation, preserving the common prefix and actual recorded allocation extent even on shrink. Failure leaves the prior pointer, length and initialized bytes intact. Newly grown safe byte storage is explicitly zero initialized.

Reallocate of an existing owner to zero follows the existing selected CRT policy: on pinned GNU/Linux it consumes the owner, clears the safe Option and returns the native OOM message. The native oracle explicitly clears its now-dangling C++ variable after the exception rather than reading/freeing it.

AlignedMemory uses the same actual owner with the existing runtime alignment validation, eliminating independent Vec over-allocation and offset traversal. Stored original provenance controls free; slices never replace the allocation pointer.

StandardMemory content equality and Debug output, ordinary/aligned owner Send+Sync+Unpin, byte initialization, reborrowed payloads and independent thread owners are regression checked. Shared Standard/Common free interoperability is tested through the actual backend under strict provenance.

The expanded exact compiler checklist preserves 427 declaration records and 167 callable records across 10 classes. Template wrapper records remain separate; all scopes and gaps stay explicit. The earlier canonical IBlock receipt remains an independent dependency, not evidence relabeled as new Standard coverage.

adaptations_and_remaining_gaps: Only the selected NATIVE memory-manager configuration is exercised. FLEXIBLE/TBB/JEMALLOC backends and arbitrary build-policy switching are not claimed.

Safe Rust byte slices initialize malloc contents and grown realloc suffixes which native leaves unspecified. Rust layout headers, layout limits and positive failure return conventions remain explicit adaptations; malloc ABI/heap accounting is not byte-for-byte native.

The glibc realloc(existing,0) exception frees the allocation but leaves the caller C++ pointer variable unchanged unless caught and repaired; the Rust safe Option is cleared to prevent a dangling safe owner. Exact pointer-variable semantics are not claimed.

Reallocation movement and physical capacity decisions are allocator dependent; only requested extent and initialized common prefix are compared. Aligned Debug now describes logical owned bytes, not incidental former Vec padding.

Standard-specific new/delete/array/placement operators, arbitrary raw void-pointer/template slot overloads, protected MMgrOpt Initialize and native mutable allocator fields/subclassing remain incomplete; no full family or global API parity is asserted.
